questions.question: For which matrices is the determinant discussed?
What does a nonzero determinant tell you about a square matrix?
options: Every entry of the matrix is nonzero.
The matrix must be the identity.

questions.question: If $\det(A)=0$ for a square matrix $A$, what is the immediate invertibility conclusion?
options: $A$ must have exactly one zero entry.

questions.question: What is $\det(I_n)$?
How does the determinant of a product relate to the determinants of the factors?
For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$, what is $\det(A)$?
What is the determinant of a triangular matrix?
options: the product of its diagonal entries
the sum of all its entries

questions.question: How does $\det(A^T)$ relate to $\det(A)$?
For a $2\times2$ matrix $A$, what is $\det(2A)$ in terms of $\det(A)$?
Which $2\times2$ matrix has determinant $1$?
Why is it misleading to treat $|A|$ exactly like the absolute value of a number?
options: For a matrix, $|A|$ means the number of rows.
For a matrix, $|A|$ is determinant notation, not a distance from zero.
For a matrix, $|A|$ is only allowed when $A$ is rectangular.
For a matrix, $|A|$ is always nonnegative.

questions.question: What does the determinant summarize in one scalar?
options: The full list of all entries of a matrix.
The order in which row operations were performed, for every possible choice of input.
Invertibility and volume scaling information of a square matrix.
The right-hand side vector of a linear system.

questions.question: Can two different square matrices have the same determinant?
options: Only if both matrices are singular.
Only if both matrices are identity matrices.
No. The determinant uniquely determines every entry.
Yes. The determinant is only one scalar summary.

questions.question: If $\det(A)=-2$ and $\det(B)=4$, what is $\det(AB)$?
For $D=\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\0&5\end{pmatrix}$, what is $\det(D)$?
Swapping two rows of a matrix multiplies its determinant by:
Why does $\det(A)=0$ suggest that the associated linear transformation loses volume?
options: A zero determinant means all lengths are doubled.
A zero determinant means every vector is sent to itself.
A zero volume scaling factor means some volume is collapsed to zero.
A zero determinant means the map is automatically nonlinear.

questions.question: Which proposed rule for determinants is false in general?
If $A$ and $B$ are square matrices and $\det(A)=0$, which conclusion follows about $AB$?
A square matrix $A$ has $\det(A)=6$. A student says $A$ cannot be invertible because the determinant is not $1$. What is wrong?
options: A determinant of $6$ means the matrix has six rows.
The determinant criterion applies only to zero matrices.
Any nonzero determinant, not only $1$, gives invertibility.
